# wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/^0.6/

## Expand description

`wiremock` provides HTTP mocking to perform black-box testing of Rust applications that
interact with third-party APIs.

It provides mocking of HTTP responses using request matching and response templating.

[§](https://docs.rs#how-to-install)How to install

Add `wiremock` to your development dependencies:

```
[dev-dependencies]
# ...
wiremock = "0.5"
```
If you are using [ cargo-edit](https://github.com/killercup/cargo-edit), run

`cargo add wiremock --dev`[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::{method, path};
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Start a background HTTP server on a random local port
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    // Arrange the behaviour of the MockServer adding a Mock:
    // when it receives a GET request on '/hello' it will respond with a 200.
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .and(path("/hello"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        // Mounting the mock on the mock server - it's now effective!
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // If we probe the MockServer using any HTTP client it behaves as expected.
    let status = reqwest::get(format!("{}/hello", &mock_server.uri()))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // If the request doesn't match any `Mock` mounted on our `MockServer` a 404 is returned.
    let status = reqwest::get(format!("{}/missing", &mock_server.uri()))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#matchers)Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.Check

[’s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html)

`Match`[§](https://docs.rs#spying)Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.

By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[§](https://docs.rs#responses)Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/struct.ResponseTemplate.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s that return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

`Request`[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`Check

[’s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`[§](https://docs.rs#test-isolation)Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn’t be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-compatibility)Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes.](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our

[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#efficiency)Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html).

Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it’s a bug: open an issue!

[§](https://docs.rs#prior-art)Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn’t been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request matching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

[§](https://docs.rs#future-evolution)Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related projects

- `stubr`- `Wiremock`- `MockServer`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [crypto](https://docs.rs/crypto/index.html)
- Utilities for dealing with crypto primitives. Sometimes we need to use these from inside WASM contracts, where crypto calculations have weak performance.
- [dispatch](https://docs.rs/dispatch/index.html)
- Dispatch system. Contains a macro for defining runtime modules and generating values representing lazy module function calls.
- [dispatch_](https://docs.rs/dispatch_context/index.html)- context
- Provides functions to interact with the dispatch context.
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/generate_genesis_config/index.html)- genesis_ - config
- Helper for generating the `RuntimeGenesisConfig`instance for presets. Helper macro allowing to construct JSON representation of partially initialized structs.
- [genesis_](https://docs.rs/genesis_builder_helper/index.html)- builder_ - helper
- Helper for implementing GenesisBuilder runtime API
Helper functions for implementing `sp_genesis_builder::GenesisBuilder`
- [inherent](https://docs.rs/inherent/index.html)
- [instances](https://docs.rs/instances/index.html)
- Some instance placeholder to be used in `frame_support::pallet`
- [migrations](https://docs.rs/migrations/index.html)
- [pallet_](https://docs.rs/pallet_macros/index.html)- macros
- Contains macro stubs for all of the `pallet::`macros
- [pallet_](https://docs.rs/pallet_prelude/index.html)- prelude
- Prelude to be used alongside pallet macro, for ease of use.
- [storage](https://docs.rs/storage/index.html)
- Stuff to do with the runtime’s storage.
- [testing_](https://docs.rs/testing_prelude/index.html)- prelude
- Prelude to be used for pallet testing, for ease of use.
- [traits](https://docs.rs/traits/index.html)
- Traits and associated utilities for use in the FRAME environment.
- [view_](https://docs.rs/view_functions/index.html)- functions
- Traits for querying pallet view functions.
- [weights](https://docs.rs/weights/index.html)
- Re-exports `sp-weights`public API, and contains benchmarked weight constants specific to FRAME.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [_std_](https://docs.rs/macro._std_enabled.html)- enabled
- [_try_](https://docs.rs/macro._try_runtime_and_std_not_enabled.html)- runtime_ - and_ - std_ - not_ - enabled
- [_try_](https://docs.rs/macro._try_runtime_enabled.html)- runtime_ - enabled

- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_err_ignore_postinfo.html)- err_ - ignore_ - postinfo
- Assert an expression returns an error specified.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_err_with_weight.html)- err_ - with_ - weight
- Assert an expression returns error with the given weight.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_error_encoded_size.html)- error_ - encoded_ - size
- Assert that the maximum encoding size does not exceed the value defined in
`MAX_MODULE_ERROR_ENCODED_SIZE`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_noop.html)- noop
- Evaluate an expression, assert it returns an expected `Err`value and that runtime storage has not been mutated (i.e. expression is a no-operation).
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_ok.html)- ok
- Panic if an expression doesn’t evaluate to `Ok`.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_storage_noop.html)- storage_ - noop
- Evaluate any expression and assert that runtime storage has not been mutated (i.e. expression is a storage no-operation).
- [build_](https://docs.rs/macro.build_struct_json_patch.html)- struct_ - json_ - patch
- Creates a JSON patch for given `struct_type`, supporting recursive field initialization.
- [construct_](https://docs.rs/macro.construct_runtime.html)- runtime
- Construct a runtime, with the given name and the given pallets.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_to_crate_version.html)- to_ - crate_ - version
- Convert the current crate version into a `CrateVersion`
- [defensive](https://docs.rs/macro.defensive.html)
- Generic function to mark an execution path as ONLY defensive.
- [defensive_](https://docs.rs/macro.defensive_assert.html)- assert
- Trigger a defensive failure if a condition is not met.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Evaluate `$x:expr`and if not true return`Err($y:expr)`.
- [fail](https://docs.rs/macro.fail.html)
- Return Err of the expression: `return Err($expression);`.
- [hypothetically](https://docs.rs/macro.hypothetically.html)
- Do something hypothetically by rolling back any changes afterwards.
- [hypothetically_](https://docs.rs/macro.hypothetically_ok.html)- ok
- Assert something to be *hypothetically*`Ok`, without actually committing it.
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_ensure_origin_with_arg_ignoring_arg.html)- ensure_ - origin_ - with_ - arg_ - ignoring_ - arg
- Simple macro to explicitly implement [EnsureOriginWithArg](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.EnsureOriginWithArg.html)to be used on any type which implements[EnsureOrigin](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.EnsureOrigin.html). This is quick and dirty, so you must use the type parameters`O`(the origin type),`T`(the argument type) and`AccountId`(if you are using the`O: ..`form).
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_filter_stack.html)- filter_ - stack
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_for_tuples_attr.html)- for_ - tuples_ - attr
- Puts the `impl_for_tuples`
- [match_](https://docs.rs/macro.match_and_insert.html)- and_ - insert
- Macro that inserts some tokens after the first match of some pattern.
- [match_](https://docs.rs/macro.match_type.html)- type - Deprecated
- Create a type which implements the `Contains`trait for a particular type with syntax similar to`matches!`.
- [match_](https://docs.rs/macro.match_types.html)- types
- Create a type which implements the `Contains`trait for a particular type with syntax similar to`matches!`.
- [ord_](https://docs.rs/macro.ord_parameter_types.html)- parameter_ - types
- Macro for easily creating a new implementation of both the `Get`and`Contains`traits. Use exactly as with`parameter_types`, only the type must be`Ord`.
- [parameter_](https://docs.rs/macro.parameter_types.html)- types
- Create new implementations of the `Get`
- [parameter_](https://docs.rs/macro.parameter_types_impl_thread_local.html)- types_ - impl_ - thread_ - local
- [runtime_](https://docs.rs/macro.runtime_print.html)- print
- Print out a formatted message.
- [std_](https://docs.rs/macro.std_enabled.html)- enabled
- Enable/disable the given code depending on
`feature = "std"`being enabled for the crate or not.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_runtime_and_std_not_enabled.html)- runtime_ - and_ - std_ - not_ - enabled
- Enable/disable the given code depending on
`all(not(feature = "try-runtime"), not(feature = "std"))`being enabled for the crate or not.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_runtime_enabled.html)- runtime_ - enabled
- Enable/disable the given code depending on
`feature = "try-runtime"`being enabled for the crate or not.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_runtime_or_std_enabled.html)- runtime_ - or_ - std_ - enabled
- Enable/disable the given code depending on
`any(feature = "try-runtime", feature = "std")`being enabled for the crate or not.
